The code itself remains within the UNTDID 4451 list accepted by BR-CL-08.

value.text: Tout retard de paiement entraîne des pénalités au taux de {lateFeeRate} l'an, exigibles le jour suivant la date de règlement figurant sur la facture, sans qu'un rappel soit nécessaire (art. L441-10 du code de commerce).
value.fallbackText: Tout retard de paiement entraîne des pénalités calculées au taux d'intérêt appliqué par la Banque centrale européenne à son opération de refinancement la plus récente, majoré de 10 points de pourcentage, exigibles le jour suivant la date de règlement figurant sur la facture, sans qu'un rappel soit nécessaire (art. L441-10 du code de commerce).
value.legalRef: C. com. art. L441-9 I al. 5, L441-10 II
value.notes: Same nuance as PMT: expected by the platform, not named by any DGFiP text found. Issue #519: fallbackText is used instead of `text` only when noteValues.lateFeeRate's last dated window has already ended and nobody has added the next one yet -- it quotes L441-10 II's own rate-setting rule verbatim (the statute itself never fixes a number, only 'the ECB's most recent refinancing rate plus 10 percentage points') rather than a pre-computed figure. No official source (Légifrance, the DGCCRF's own 'Délais de paiement' fiche pratique) requires a numeric-only mention; a stale number would be strictly worse than restating the rule the statute itself uses.

value.legalRef: C. com. art. L441-9 I al. 5 ; formulation : service-public F31808
value.notes: Only AAB is backed by a DGFiP rule found (G1.52). No specific wording is imposed by law for the two mentions above (PMT/PMD): only the CONTENT is (an amount, a rate). The « néant » of the discount is the wording prescribed by administrative doctrine (entreprendre.service-public.gouv.fr, sheet F31808), not by a statute.

lateFeeRate.notes: ECB MRO 2,40 % since 17 June 2026, hence in force as of 1 July → 12,40 %. validTo caps this at the NEXT scheduled semi-annual check (L441-10 II reads the rate again on 1 January) rather than left open-ended. Issue #519: the 1 January 2027 rate is NOT YET officially published as of this fix (2026-09-28) -- the ECB Governing Council decision covering that date is expected 17 December 2026, the last scheduled meeting before it, and a mid-September 2026 rise to 2.65 % has already happened but only takes effect for THIS table on the next 1 January reading, never retroactively into the current half-year (L441-10 II reads the rate on 1 January/1 July only). Add the real 2027-01-01 entry as soon as the December decision is published -- until then, an invoice issued on or after 2027-01-01 prints PMD's own `fallbackText` (schema.ts) instead of a stale or invented figure. The 90-day canary in `data/all.spec.ts` exists so this cannot be forgotten.

mentions.notes: The three mentions from article L441-9 I al. 5 of the Code de commerce, in a single sentence: « Elle précise les conditions d'escompte applicables en cas de paiement à une date antérieure […], le taux des pénalités exigibles le jour suivant la date de règlement inscrite sur la facture ainsi que le montant de l'indemnité forfaitaire pour frais de recouvrement due au créancier en cas de retard de paiement. » All three are statutory: true -- the law supplies the value, the user has nothing to enter; a stipulated rate different from the supplementary one would itself be a commercial choice, hence absent here. Sources checked on 2026-08-29 (carried over from the pre-refactor git tag, compliance/profiles/data/fr.ts): C. com. art. L441-9, L441-10 II, D441-5 (via codes.droit.org, consolidation as of 21/08/2026 -- legifrance returns 403 to automated requests); entreprendre.service-public.gouv.fr F31808 and F23211; ECB, key interest rates. NUANCE WORTH KNOWING (carried over from the tag): superpdp rejects invoices by invoking a rule « BR-FR-05 » that cannot be found in the DGFiP's external specifications v3.2 (French rules there are numbered G1.xx/G2.xx/G6.xx/P1.xx), and BG-1 is 0..n there, hence optional -- carrying them in BG-1 nonetheless remains compliant (all three codes are in the UNTDID 4451 list accepted by BR-CL-08) and this is what satisfies both the legal obligation and the platform's own check. The supplementary rate (lateFeeRate) is the ECB refinancing rate plus 10 points, read on 1 January for the first half-year and on 1 July for the second (L441-10 II) -- FROZEN AT ISSUANCE: a July invoice keeps the July rate forever, never recomputed as of the reading date. Legal floor: a stipulated rate may not be lower than 3 times the statutory interest rate (8,25 % in the second half of 2026 per service-public); the supplementary rate is well above it, so applying it satisfies the floor with no calculation needed. TO BE MAINTAINED TWICE A YEAR -- when the ECB moves, ADD a dated entry to noteValues.lateFeeRate rather than MODIFYING the last one: every invoice is still judged on the rate actually in force on its own issue date.

provenance.sourceText: Code général des impôts, art. 289 E : « Les données des factures électroniques émises en application du I de l'article 289 bis sont transmises à l'administration par la plateforme agréée choisie par l'assujetti. » — texte consolidé en vigueur, issu de la LOI n° 2026-103 du 19 février 2026, art. 123, lu directement à la source primaire (codes.droit.org, PDF officiel du Code général des impôts, 15 Mo, HTTP 200, extrait via pdftotext -layout). Légifrance and the JORF were retried the same day and, from this environment, returned either a Cloudflare wall ("Just a moment...") or an empty JavaScript shell — never the text itself.

facts.notes: Art. 289 bis I mandates e-invoicing through an accredited platform (PDP) between two VAT-liable persons established in France ('B2B domestic') — the scope this fact covers. Art. 289 E (quoted above) then puts the duty to TRANSMIT that invoice's data to the tax administration on the PDP itself, never on the issuing company — exactly what `dischargedBy: "transport"` expresses: this catalog has nothing to enqueue for a B2B-domestic French invoice, because the transport that already carries it (transports/pdp-transport.ts, proven live end to end on 2026-08-29) is itself the party the law makes responsible on the administration side. `providerId` names a `transports/transport-registry.ts` id here ("pdp"), never a `DeclarationProviderRegistry` one — see schema.ts's own header on this deliberate field reuse. `applicableFrom` is deliberately omitted: art. 289 bis's own size-tiered rollout (large/mid companies first, small/micro a year later) is fixed by décret n° 2022-1299 as later modified, and by LOI n° 2026-103's own art. 123 transitional provisions — neither was readable in brut text from this environment on 2026-09-16 (a Légifrance JORFTEXT/LODA id for the décret, and a guessed codes.droit.org codified-article path, were both tried; the former returned only Légifrance's own navigation shell, the latter 404'd) — so no date is asserted, honestly, rather than guessed from secondary commentary.

facts.periodicity: Periodic, aggregated declaration (CGI art. 290 II/III) — never a real-time, per-invoice call; this catalog's own send-time trigger (report-on-send.ts) excludes every SCOPED fact for exactly this reason (no per-invoice B2B/B2C/domestic/export classifier exists yet in this codebase — see registry.ts#obligationFor's own header). The exact frequency (daily/10-day/monthly) is not sourced in brut text from this environment.

provenance.resolutionNote: CGI art. 290 I/II/III, read in brut (codes.droit.org, official CGI PDF, pdftotext -layout, 2026-09-16), confirms a periodic obligation — separate from 289 bis/289 E above — owed by the assujetti itself, to communicate to the administration the data of B2C-domestic, export, and intra-EU operations: « Les assujettis [...] communiquent à l'administration [...] les données relatives aux opérations suivantes » (the [...] are the researcher's own, marking genuinely elided text within the same brut extraction, never an invented quote). What is NOT yet settled, and blocks this fact from being `legal`: (1) the applicability calendar by company size (décret n° 2022-1299 as modified, and LOI n° 2026-103 art. 123's own transitional provisions) — Légifrance/JORF (Cloudflare wall), BOFiP (empty JS shell), and economie.gouv.fr (403) were all retried on 2026-09-16 with no brut text obtained; (2) the exact I/II/III sub-paragraph text beyond the fragment quoted above. To settle: find a working brut route into Légifrance's LODA/JORF for this décret and its later modifying texts, or a mirror serving the JORF publication as plain text/PDF the way codes.droit.org does for the codified CGI. `providerId: "fr-ereporting"` is a deliberately UNREGISTERED placeholder — no `DeclarationProvider` implements it (`documents-core.module.ts` only ever registers `pt-at`) — named here only so the obligation stays visible as DATA (company/channels settings screen, a future declarations UI) rather than absent from the catalog entirely, the same 'named before it's wired' convention `b2g-routing/data/pt.json`'s `fe-ap` and France's own pre-wiring `chorus-pro` already used.

What is NOT settled: this research pass captured only that characterization, never art. 290 A's own verbatim wording (unlike 289 E/290 above), nor its applicability calendar — the same Légifrance/BOFiP/economie.gouv.fr blockers logged on the other two facts applied here too, retried on 2026-09-16. To settle: read art. 290 A's own text in brut (the same codes.droit.org CGI PDF already has it — a targeted re-read was not done this pass) and confirm the calendar the same way the other two facts need. `providerId` is the SAME unregistered 'fr-ereporting' placeholder as the fact above — one conceptual French e-reporting obligation, several CGI articles, no implemented provider for either slice yet.

categories.notes: Retrieved curl -A "Mozilla/5.0" https://codes.droit.org/PDF/Code%20g%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20imp%C3%B4ts.pdf (HTTP 200, 15 302 264 bytes), pdftotext -layout — codes.droit.org is already this codebase's own established Légifrance mirror for FR provenance (built from the official Légifrance API, per the PDF's own front matter; already cited this way in `correction-routes/data/fr.json`, `country-policy/data/fr.json`, `tax/tax-systems/data/fr.json`, `mentions/data/fr.json`, `vat-rates/data/fr.json` and others), edition '2026-09-01' per the PDF's own header. Cloudflare challenge page for every article URL tried) and that an earlier attempt at codes.droit.org used an INVENTED path and 404'd — the real path, found from the site's own index page (https://codes.droit.org/, listing every code's real PDF filename), is the one used here. provenance.sourceText: 2 sexies. Pour les livraisons et les prestations de façon portant sur des déchets neufs d'industrie et des matières de récupération, la taxe est acquittée par le destinataire ou le preneur qui dispose d'un numéro d'identification à la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée en France.

provenance.sourceText: 2 septies. Pour les transferts de quotas autorisant les exploitants à émettre des gaz à effet de serre, au sens de l'article 3 de la directive 2003/87/ CE du Parlement européen et du Conseil du 13 octobre 2003 établissant un système d'échange de quotas d'émission de gaz à effet de serre dans la Communauté et modifiant la directive 96/61/ CE du Conseil, et d'autres unités pouvant être utilisées par les opérateurs en vue de se conformer à cette directive, la taxe est acquittée par l'assujetti bénéficiaire du transfert. Shares the `greenhouse-gas-and-energy-certificates` key with IT (DPR 633/1972 art. 17 comma 6 lett. d-bis/d-ter), DE (§ 13b Abs. 2 Nr. 6) and PT (CIVA art. 2.º n.º 1 alínea l) — PT's own scope is narrower, GHG allowances only; see PT's own fact).

provenance.sourceText: Pour les livraisons de gaz naturel ou d'électricité mentionnées au b du même III, ainsi que pour les services définis au 13° de l'article 259 B qui leur sont directement liés, la taxe est acquittée par l'acquéreur qui dispose d'un numéro d'identification à la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée en France, y compris lorsque son fournisseur est établi en France.

categories.notes: Same retrieval as `construction-subcontracting` above. This is the SECOND sentence of 2 quinquies; the FIRST sentence ('Pour les livraisons mentionnées au III de l'article 258, la taxe est acquittée par l'acquéreur ... lorsque son fournisseur est établi hors de France') is a genuinely cross-border case (an explicit 'établi hors de France' condition on the supplier) and is NOT modeled here for the same reason DE's own § 13b Abs. 2 Nr. 1/Nr. 5 Buchst. a) and PL are excluded — see `data/de.json`'s own file-level notes. This second sentence is the one that explicitly says 'y compris lorsque son fournisseur est établi en France' (including when the supplier is established in France), which is what makes it a genuinely DOMESTIC case. Condition NOT modeled: the buyer must hold a French VAT identification number. Shares the `gas-and-electricity-to-reseller` key with IT (DPR 633/1972 art. 17 comma 6 lett. d-quater) and DE (§ 13b Abs. 2 Nr. 5 Buchst. b).

provenance.sourceText: 2 octies. Pour les services de communications électroniques, à l'exclusion de ceux soumis à la taxe mentionnée à l'article L. 453-1 du code des impositions sur les biens et services, la taxe est acquittée par l'acquéreur qui dispose d'un numéro d'identification à la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée en France.

categories.notes: Same retrieval as `construction-subcontracting` above. Excludes services subject to the tax mentioned at Code des impositions sur les biens et services art. L. 453-1 — that carve-out is NOT itself retrieved or modeled here. Condition NOT modeled: the buyer must hold a French VAT identification number. domesticReverseCharge.notes: Retrieved curl -A "Mozilla/5.0" https://codes.droit.org/PDF/Code%20g%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral%20des%20imp%C3%B4ts.pdf (HTTP 200, 15 302 264 bytes, edition 2026-09-01), pdftotext -layout, 2026-09-13. This wave's own task brief said France was 'not established' as of the brief's own writing and listed three failed FR retrieval routes (a Cloudflare-walled Légifrance permalink, an INVENTED codes.droit.org path that 404'd, and a BOFiP page that returned HTTP 200 with a page shell but no article text) — none of those routes was repeated: the real codes.droit.org path was found from that site's own index page rather than guessed, and the retrieved body was checked to actually carry CGI art. 283's full numbered-paragraph text (not a shell) before anything was quoted from it. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: CGI art. 283, 1 and 2 (the general reverse-charge rule for a supply made by a trader established OUTSIDE France — genuinely cross-border, already the CROSS-BORDER branch's own territory), 2 bis (intra-Community acquisitions — cross-border by definition), 2 ter (art. 258 D I 2° deliveries — not itself retrieved, so its domestic/cross-border character was not established either way and it is left out rather than guessed), 2 decies (a ministerial emergency-decree POWER to add further categories, not itself a category), and 3/4/4 bis/4 ter/5 (liability for VAT WRONGLY invoiced or for a fraudulent chain — a different legal concept, 'who owes tax because of a billing error or a fraud they knew about', not 'the buyer is liable by the nature of the transaction'). field.label: Supply type
field.helpText: Whether this line is a delivery of goods or a supply of services — used to derive BT-23 ("cadre de facturation") on a French invoice. Optional: leave unset if unsure.

countryFields.notes: France's FIRST real field-overlay file — see this directory's own `data/all.ts` header for why it shipped empty until now. Adds `supplyType` as an OPTIONAL 'select' subfield of `invoice.lines`, consumed by `formats/semantic/business-process.ts#resolveFrenchBusinessProcessCode` (via `formats/shared-build.ts#extractLines`) to derive BT-23's own goods/services/mixed category (CGI ann. II art. 242 nonies A, I, 8° bis — see `content-requirements/data/fr.json` for the sourced, dated citation and the date this becomes binding). A LINE subfield, not a document-level field: BT-23's own category genuinely depends on what each line actually contains (a mixed invoice derives 'mixte' automatically the moment both values appear across its lines), which a single document-wide toggle could not express without asking the user to pre-summarize their own invoice. Deliberately OPTIONAL — a French invoice with no line declaring this still builds (M1, the value that asserts nothing false about the content, per `business-process.ts`'s own documented default); this field only lets a seller be MORE precise (B1/S1) when they choose to say so, never forces a new required field onto an existing workflow. Labels are plain data (see `descriptors/types.ts`'s own comment on `DocumentTypeDescriptor.label`: the frontend renders `field.label`/`option.label` directly, never through `t()`), so this needed no i18n locale entry — consistent with every other field label already in `invoice.descriptor.ts`.

provenance.sourceText: 8° bis L'information selon laquelle les opérations donnant lieu à facture sont constituées exclusivement de livraisons de biens ou exclusivement de prestations de services ou sont constituées de ces deux catégories d'opérations ; (CGI, annexe II, art. 242 nonies A, I, 8° bis)

facts.notes: The exact text was found in the consolidated PDF « Code général des impôts, annexe II » (codes.droit.org, the Légifrance mirror already used for ../../mentions/data/fr.json — Légifrance itself returns 403 to automated requests, see that file), the version shown as last updated 2026-07-29, checked on 2026-08-31. The pre-refactor git tag `avant-refonte-documents` (compliance/providers/format/providers.ts, P2-T08) carried only a PARAPHRASE of this 8° bis (« the machine translation of the statutory mention 8° bis... ») with no verbatim citation and no check date; the text above is the exact citation, verified for this task, that was missing. The effective DATE (2026-09-01) is not carried by article 242 nonies A itself (an implementing decree, with no calendar clause of its own in the consolidated text) but by the mandatory e-invoicing regime it equips — CGI art. 289 bis/290, already sourced and dated (checked 2026-08-28) in ../../transports/channel-policy/data/fr.json for the same milestone. BT-23 (EN 16931, UBL cbc:ProfileID / CII BusinessProcessSpecifiedDocumentContextParameter/ID) is the machine translation of this 8° bis — the closed value list French law imposes exists nowhere in a text cited here word for word (B1/S1/M1/...): it comes from the DGFiP's own external specifications v3.2, not from the CGI — see formats/semantic/business-process.ts's own header, which already carries it and is not duplicated here.

requiredClientIdentifiers.label: SIRET
requiredClientIdentifiers.why: Chorus Pro identifies every public-sector recipient by its SIRET (the 14-digit establishment number) — the SAME "LEGAL_ID" scheme this catalog already uses for a French client's own identifier (see country-identifiers/data/fr.json, which already accepts both the 9-digit SIREN and the 14-digit SIRET). A government client with no SIRET on file cannot be routed to Chorus Pro at all.

requiredDocumentFields.label: Code service (destinataire)
requiredDocumentFields.why: Chorus Pro routes an invoice inside a public entity by a "code service" identifying which department/service ordered it — not every public entity requires one (it depends on how that entity organized its own Chorus Pro account), so this stays optional rather than a hard block. Reuses the SAME generic `buyerReference` field the DE/XRechnung rule below also reads (`formats/shared-build.ts#extractBuyerReference`, `country-fields/data/de.json`'s own header) — a deliberate modeling choice, not a coincidence: both are "which unit inside the recipient should receive this" facts, even though French doctrine calls it "code service" and German law calls it "Leitweg-ID".

L. 2192-1 (LOI n°2022-1157 du 16 août 2022, art. 26) : « Les titulaires de marchés conclus avec les personnes morales de droit public, ainsi que leurs sous-traitants admis au paiement direct, transmettent leurs factures sous forme électronique. » Art. L. 2192-2 (même loi) : « Les personnes morales de droit public acceptent les factures transmises sous forme électronique par les titulaires de marchés mentionnés à l'article L. 2192-1 et leurs sous-traitants admis au paiement direct. » Art. L. 2192-5 (LOI n°2026-103 du 19 février 2026, art. 123) : « Une solution mutualisée, mise à disposition par l'Etat et dénommée " portail public de facturation ", permet le dépôt, la réception et la transmission des factures sous forme électronique [...]. Pour la mise en œuvre des obligations fixées à la sous-section 1 de la présente section, utilisent le portail public de facturation : 1° L'Etat, les collectivités territoriales et les établissements publics ; 2° Les titulaires de marchés conclus avec un acheteur mentionné au 1° ainsi que leurs sous-traitants admis au paiement direct. »

b2gRouting.notes: READ DIRECTLY on 2026-09-01 at codes.droit.org (official PDF of the Code de la commande publique, https://codes.droit.org/PDF/Code%20de%20la%20commande%20publique.pdf, articles L. 2192-1/L. 2192-2/L. 2192-5 — see sourceText above, a verbatim citation extracted from the PDF itself, not paraphrased). Légifrance kept refusing every automated request (the same wall country-policy/data/fr.json and country-identifiers/data/fr.json already document for this specific site). EUROPEAN BASELINE common to the three countries in this wave: directive 2014/55/EU, art. 7 (EUR-Lex, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32014L0055, checked 2026-09-01): « Member States shall ensure that contracting authorities and contracting entities receive and process electronic invoices which comply with the European standard on electronic invoicing [...] » — this directive imposes RECEIPT by the contracting authority, never issuance by the supplier; it is art. L. 2192-1 et seq. above that, under French law, impose electronic issuance by the contract holder IN RETURN. `transportId: "chorus-pro"` DELIBERATELY references a channel that does NOT EXIST in `transports/transport-registry.ts` (email/pdp/ksef/sdi only) — that is this model's own thesis (see actions/invoice-actions.ts's own header): the legal text above names "le portail public de facturation" (operated under the "Chorus Pro" brand by the AIFE — a well-known fact, documented elsewhere in this repository at `documentation/compliance/FR-France.md`, but NOT re-confirmed at its primary source by THIS task, for lack of access: chorus-pro.gouv.fr/portail.chorus-pro.gouv.fr are JavaScript applications that render no text to a plain request), never one of the four channels already implemented here — sending must therefore REFUSE, by naming it, rather than silently routing to a channel (email, pdp) the text does not designate. `formatSyntax: "facturx"` is a DELIBERATE choice but NOT re-verified against Chorus Pro's own documentation (the Chorus Pro community site, communaute.chorus-pro.gouv.fr, rendered no usable text to this task either): Factur-X is the hybrid PDF/XML EN 16931 format this repository already builds (`formats/facturx-provider.ts`) and the format already used for the existing French PDP channel (`transports/pdp-transport.ts`) — a choice consistent with what already exists rather than an independently sourced fact about exactly what Chorus Pro accepts (UBL is also probably accepted; not settled here).

provenance.sourceText: Code de commerce, art. L. 441-10, I: "Le délai convenu entre les parties pour régler les sommes dues ne peut dépasser soixante jours après la date d'émission de la facture. Par dérogation, un délai maximal de quarante-cinq jours fin de mois après la date d'émission de la facture peut être convenu entre les parties, sous réserve que ce délai soit expressément stipulé par contrat et qu'il ne constitue pas un abus manifeste à l'égard du créancier."

paymentTerms.notes: Read directly at codes.droit.org (Code de commerce PDF, https://codes.droit.org/PDF/Code%20de%20commerce.pdf). Absent a contrary agreement the term cannot exceed thirty days after receipt of the goods or performance of the service (first paragraph of the same article). A periodic invoice (CGI art. 289, I, 3) is capped at forty-five days net, which this fact does not model.
